source: Cloud Carbon Footprint methodology (Azure avg min/max 0.78/3.76 W per vCPU, AWS 0.74/3.5, memory 0.392 W/GB), cloudcarbonfootprint.org/docs/methodology (accessed 2026-11-20)
calculation_or_assumption: Node = 16 vCPU + 64 GB (data dictionary), at 35 % CPU, excl. PUE. Pipeline uses daily AvgCpuPercent.

source: Assumption: datacentre GPUs of the 250-300 W class idle at roughly 10-25 % of TDP (vendor datasheets / nvidia-smi idle readings); to be measured on gpu-ml-01.; Cloud Carbon Footprint methodology (Azure avg min/max 0.78/3.76 W per vCPU, AWS 0.74/3.5, memory 0.392 W/GB), cloudcarbonfootprint.org/docs/methodology (accessed 2026-11-20)
calculation_or_assumption: At the observed 9 % GPU utilisation: idle W + 9 % x (300 W - idle) + host 8 vCPU/56 GB, excl. PUE. At full load: about 0.33-0.37 kWh.

source: Cloud Carbon Footprint storage coefficients (HDD 0.65 Wh/TB-h, SSD 1.2 Wh/TB-h) x replication factor, cloudcarbonfootprint.org/docs/methodology (accessed 2026-11-20)
calculation_or_assumption: low = HDD, no replication (0.65*24/1e6); mid = SSD x 1.5 replication; high = SSD x 3 replication.

source: Google (2025): median Gemini Apps text prompt 0.24 Wh incl. idle capacity and datacentre overhead, cloud.google.com/blog/products/infrastructure/measuring-the-environmental-impact-of-ai-inference; OpenAI CEO statement 0.34 Wh per ChatGPT query (via CBS News, 2025-08-21) (accessed 2026-11-20)
calculation_or_assumption: Gateway data average about 1,800 tokens per request; 0.2 Wh/1000 tokens gives about 0.36 Wh per request, in line with both disclosures. Applies to LARGE models, incl. datacentre overhead (no extra PUE). Cached input tokens weighted at 10 %. Small models: x 0.25 (0.1-0.4).

source: Google 2025 (0.24 Wh per median prompt) and OpenAI (0.34 Wh per query), see energy_per_1000_tokens
calculation_or_assumption: One chat message in ChatGPT Team / Claude Team / Copilot. High end: long-context and reasoning answers.

source: Microsoft: newest datacentre generation design PUE 1.12 (azure.microsoft.com blog); CCF uses 1.185 for Azure; high = Uptime Institute 2024 Europe average 1.45; Assumption for a Swiss colocation hoster; high = Uptime Institute 2024 global average 1.56, intelligence.uptimeinstitute.com (accessed 2026-11-20)
calculation_or_assumption: Applied per provider: Azure 1.185, AWS 1.135, Swiss hoster 1.4 (mid). Provider figures are design/fleet averages and not audited per region, so the high end uses the Uptime industry average. AI per-token factor already includes datacentre overhead.

source: Headcount (FTE): extra/headcount.csv, Nov 2024 to Aug 2026 (CAGR); AI token usage: ai_usage.csv, Nov-Aug year on year, endless loop T-1212 excluded; Cloud services: azure/aws/hoster line items, Nov-Aug year on year; Servers: Nov-Aug year on year; vm-test step (T-1058) excluded; Production platform 24 nodes: it_tickets.csv T-1261 (baseline average 18.6 nodes); Microsoft 365 price 14 USD: README list prices (12.50 -> 14 USD from 2026-07-01); Copilot Business 21 USD: README list prices (baseline average 23.2 USD; promo 18 USD Jul-Dec 2026 ignored, conservative)
calculation_or_assumption: Cost growth per year without the package (CAGR over 3 years), built bottom-up: Headcount (FTE) +4.6% per year (AI seats, SaaS licences); AI token usage +82.0% per year (AI API (gateway)); Cloud services +11.8% per year (Cloud excl. dp-prod); Servers +10.6% per year (vm-app, db-fin, gpu-ml); Production platform 24 nodes x 1.29 from Oct 2026 (dp-prod); Microsoft 365 price 14 USD x 1.012 on SaaS (SaaS); Copilot Business 21 USD x 0.940 on AI seats (AI subscriptions); Trend damping year 2 at 1/2, year 3 at 1/4 of the observed rate (AI, cloud, servers); Range low = growth capped at FTE; high = observed trends x 1.5 (all); Package ramp-up 85% of savings in year 1, 100 % after (with package). Forecast 2028/29 mid: CHF 652,065 without vs 428,392 with the package.
